setup: Set the seat so your knee keeps a slight bend with the pedal at its lowest point, and the seat level with your hip when you stand beside the bike.
Sit tall, place your feet on the pedals, and take the moving handles with a relaxed grip.
steps: Start pedalling and let your arms push and pull the handles in time with your legs: push with the arm on the side of the leg that's pushing down.
Drive through the whole foot and keep the effort shared between your legs and arms.
Go harder by pedalling and pushing faster: the fan's resistance rises with your speed, so there is no resistance setting to change.
Ease off to a slow pedal to recover between hard efforts, and keep going for the planned time, distance or calories.
instructions.breathing: Breathe steadily through the work; on hard sprints, breathe faster rather than holding your breath.

common_faults.fault: Letting the arms ride along while the legs do all the work
common_faults.correction: Push and pull the handles on purpose, matching each arm to the opposite pedal stroke.

common_faults.fault: Starting a sprint flat out and fading within seconds
common_faults.correction: Build to your target pace over the first few seconds and hold an effort you can keep for the whole interval.
Sit up, keep the chest open and the shoulders away from the ears.

precautions: Let the pedals and handles slow down before getting off: they keep moving after you stop pushing.
Build up sprint intervals gradually, since all-out efforts on an air bike raise the heart rate quickly.

name: Air Bike
summary: Pedal a fan-resisted bike while pushing and pulling its moving handles, so the arms and legs share the work and resistance rises with effort.
